title: Reward Inflation: A Healthy Stimulus for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.02545v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reward serves as the primary learning signal in reinforcement learning (RL). However, while reward magnitudes are typically held fixed throughout training, their temporal modulation remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose reward inflation, a gradual scaling of rewards over the course of training, and show that it can act as a healthy stimulus for RL. Theoretically, reward inflation induces an implicit recency weighting that upweights recent transitions during policy updates, enabling faster adaptation. We further show that, by sustaining gradient signals as the policy saturates, reward inflation suppresses the emergence of dormant neurons and helps preserve plasticity. Empirical results on ALE games and MuJoCo tasks corroborate these findings, showing that an appropriate level of reward inflation benefits a broad range of tasks. translated_title: 奖励通胀：强化学习的健康刺激剂
translated_abstract: 奖励是强化学习（RL）中的主要学习信号。然而，尽管奖励的大小通常在整个训练过程中保持固定，但其时间上的调制却一直缺乏充分研究。在本文中，我们提出了“奖励通胀”，即在训练过程中逐渐放大奖励的尺度，并证明它可以作为强化学习的一种健康刺激。从理论上讲，奖励通胀引入了一种隐式的近期性加权，在策略更新时对最近的转移赋予更高的权重，从而实现更快的适应。我们进一步证明，通过在策略趋于饱和时维持梯度信号，奖励通胀能够抑制休眠神经元的出现，并有助于保持网络的可塑性。在ALE游戏和MuJoCo任务上的实证结果证实了这些发现，表明适当程度的奖励通胀对广泛的任务都有益处。最后，我们介绍了Fed，一种能够动态调整通胀水平的自适应变体……
tldr: 提出奖励通胀方法，通过在训练中逐渐放大奖励实现隐式近期加权，加速策略适应、抑制休眠神经元并保持网络可塑性，在ALE游戏和MuJoCo任务上显著提升强化学习性能。
en_tdlr: Proposes reward inflation, a gradual scaling of rewards during training that induces implicit recency weighting, enabling faster adaptation, suppressing dormant neurons, and preserving plasticity, with benefits demonstrated across ALE games and MuJoCo tasks.
